name: 🧩 Pluggable Chrome Architecture
description:
Architettura chrome pluggable: `ChromeHost` con regioni left/right/top/bottom, provider built-in, migrazione workspace tree in `WorkspacesContainerProvider`, dynamic action registry, host API per actions/overlay/regions, placeholder token system, plugin semplici da config e runtime WASM.

═══ THE PLUGIN STORY ON ONE PAGE — the map, not the status (2026-09-01) ═══
Full version, with the reasoning: docs/chrome-and-ui.md, the section right after "How to find
things". Read that before planning anything here. Every id below was read, not recalled.

WHERE THIS IS GOING, in P022's own words: a plugin author writes their interface the way they would
in Flutter or SwiftUI, and gets EXACTLY what the app's own chrome gets — same widgets, same prefix+/
picker, same menus, focus and policy. If a plugin ends up with a poorer version of a shipped
feature, that phase has failed regardless of what loads.

THE THREE WAYS A PLUGIN PUTS SOMETHING ON SCREEN (decided in chrome-and-ui §2.7 / R6, older than
P097). A plugin never puts a surface in the tree itself; it OFFERS one and the host attaches it.
1. REQUESTED — a modal or dropdown that asks a question and returns a typed answer. The host owns
   stacking, focus trap, Escape, click-outside, placement. P035/T065.
2. CONTRIBUTED INTO A REGION — a panel, toolbar or status segment seated in the chrome. Possible
   today; add/move is P035/T064.
3. ITS OWN NAMED SURFACE — a panel of its own design, addressed by name and opened by an action the
   way heca.expose is. ⚠️ This was tracked NOWHERE; folded into P035/T065 on 2026-09-01.

WHAT A NAMED SURFACE INHERITS — only ATTACHING was ever missing. Opening is an ordinary action
carrying the name (toggle_layer { name = … }), user-rebindable and reachable from palette and RPC.
Its own keys live in a [[keys.surface]] block under its name, consulted before the global map. The
way out is free and unremovable: the `layer` floor binds Escape plus q/Ctrl+q to close_overlay,
declared once for every layer — and those keys do not exist while no layer is up, so `:q` still
quits vim. Input, hints, layout, paint and z follow from being a node in the one tree (P097).

HOW A PLUGIN WRITES WHAT GOES INSIDE — BUILT, and it is not hand-written JSON:
  heca-view               the MODEL — serde and nothing else; a plugin depends on this alone
  heca-view/src/build.rs  the TYPED SDK — one Rust type per kind, so the compiler refuses what the
                          widget cannot do. This is what an author writes.
  heca-view-realize       the ONE bridge — realize(...), below `heca`
It crosses as data because of the SANDBOX, not because of WASM: a plugin cannot hand us a closure, a
signal or a pointer to a live widget. A press comes back as an Intent (name + args). Consequence to
design around: our chrome updates in place through signals; a plugin's change is a new description —
fine for a panel or dialog, not for something changing many times a second.

WHAT IS MISSING, AND WHERE IT IS TRACKED
- Other languages: generated type definitions from the closed WidgetKind::ALL list — F003/P001/T006.
  Today a Rust author gets editor help; a JS or Python author gets nothing. This is the gap between
  "a plugin CAN do this" and "anyone can write a plugin".
- The vocabulary's holes: 13 of 46 widgets have no described form, and a context menu has no
  described declaration — P097/T501. ⚠️ Corrected 2026-09-01: a menu is a DECLARATION ATTACHED TO A
  NODE, like a press or a hint — never a widget kind an author assembles and positions.
- The proof: rebuild one of our own overlays using only what a plugin can write — P097/T502. ⚠️ Its
  text still names LayerContent, deleted in P097/T494; read it as "the described path". Until this
  lands, "a plugin can add an overlay" is an intention, not a fact.
- No host-only exceptions: the rule is compile-enforced per builder; the AUDIT proving the host-only
  list is only the legitimate cases has not been done — F004/P084/T398.
- The boundary itself: loading someone else's code, the event bus, region contributions and action
  registration across it — P022, which says outright it has NO REAL SPEC YET and needs a discovery
  pass before it can be planned. It is the least defined thing in this feature.

THE PLUGIN THAT NEEDS NO CODE AT ALL — P053, plugins from config.toml. A large share of plugins add
a command that runs a program, a panel in a region, a menu entry and a key. None of that is logic:
it is a text file declaring what exists and where it appears, in the same shapes our own defaults
use, merged by the same per-key rules so a user can override any of it. Two things follow: declaring
an action there makes it reachable by key, mouse and script at once, so a plugin cannot trap a
feature behind its own button; and everything declared is known BEFORE the plugin is loaded, so the
palette can list it and the keymap can bind it without running anything.
